intro: Customs and border protection officers read people, apply complex rules and decide quickly, skills that law enforcement and compliance value. The closest of the 25 careers below is Compliance Officers, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $80,730, and most options need no new degree.
why_it_works: Every inspection means judging whether a story adds up, explaining rules to travelers and staying calm in tense moments. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 3.88 out of 5 for this job and judgment at 3.62. Investigation, inspection and police supervision draw on the same skills. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Federal experience counts for many compliance and investigation roles; describe the regulations you enforced.
Police and detective supervisors earn $106,040 and are an 81% match.
Customs Brokers are an 80% match if you want to use your trade knowledge in the private sector.

faq.q: What jobs can former customs and border protection officers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Compliance Officers (89%), private detectives and investigators (86%) and police and detective supervisors (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Government property inspectors are also 81% matched, with a median of $80,730 for their broader BLS group.

faq.q: Which jobs for customs officers pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Air Traffic Controllers at $148,080, Compliance Managers at $141,900 and police and detective supervisors at $106,040, according to BLS May 2025 data. Compliance management usually needs a bachelor's degree, and air traffic control requires FAA training.

faq.q: Do customs officers need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than customs and border protection officers already have. A bachelor's degree is common in compliance roles, held by 38% of workers in the closest match, but your federal enforcement experience often counts as much as formal education.

faq.q: What skills should customs officers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are systems evaluation, systems analysis, operations analysis and complex problem solving. Coordination already rates 3.38 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so analyzing systems and data is the main step toward compliance and investigation roles.
